questions.question: Q1. What distinguishes 4D printing from 3D printing?

answers.b: The printed object is designed to change shape or function over time.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Color is not the defining factor.
explanations.b: Correct — The '4th dimension' is time, meaning the object transforms in response to stimuli.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Speed is not the primary distinction.

questions.question: Q2. The WLF equation characterizes which of the following?

answers.a: The glass transition and viscosity shifts.
answers.b: The tensile strength of the polymer.
answers.d: The color change under UV light.

explanations.a: Correct — The WLF equation characterizes the glass transition and viscosity changes.

questions.question: Q3. The Shape Fixity Ratio (R_f) measures:

answers.a: How fast the material breaks under stress.
answers.b: How well the temporary shape holds without an external load.
answers.c: The maximum temperature the material can withstand.

explanations.b: Correct — Shape fixity quantifies how well the temporary shape is maintained.

questions.question: Q4. Which stimulus is typically used to trigger shape recovery in thermo-responsive SMPs?

explanations.a: Incorrect — This applies to magnetically-actuated structures.
explanations.b: Incorrect — This applies to photo-responsive polymers.
explanations.c: Correct — Heat triggers the shape recovery in thermo-responsive SMPs.
explanations.d: Incorrect — This applies to hygroscopic structures.

questions.question: Q5. Why is the low thermal efficiency (1-5%) of SMPs acceptable in biomedical applications?

answers.a: Because human body heat acts as a free trigger.
answers.b: Because biomedical devices don't need to move.
answers.d: Because they are cheaper to manufacture.

explanations.a: Correct — Body heat (37°C) provides the necessary thermal energy for free.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Disposability is not related to thermal efficiency.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Manufacturing cost is independent of thermal efficiency here.

questions.question: Q6. What is the Glass Transition Temperature (T_g)?

answers.a: The point where the polymer evaporates.
answers.b: The temperature at which a polymer shifts from a glassy state to a rubbery state.
answers.c: The temperature where the polymer crystallizes into a solid.
answers.d: The maximum heating threshold before the material catches fire.

explanations.b: Correct — T_g is the transition boundary between glassy and rubbery states.
explanations.c: Incorrect — This is the crystallization temperature.
explanations.d: Incorrect — This is the degradation temperature.

questions.question: Q7. In the context of shape memory polymers, what is the role of 'netpoints'?

answers.c: They provide the elastic restoring force to remember the permanent shape.
answers.d: They absorb moisture to expand the polymer.

explanations.b: Incorrect — Switching segments determine the temporary shape.
explanations.c: Correct — Crosslinked netpoints lock in the permanent shape and provide entropic spring-back.
explanations.d: Incorrect — This relates to hydrogel swelling.

questions.question: Q8. What happens to an amorphous polymer's relaxation time as its temperature rises significantly above T_g?

answers.d: It drops to exactly zero immediately.

explanations.a: Correct — The polymer chains become highly mobile, reducing the time needed to relax stress.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Increased heat increases mobility, lowering relaxation time.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Relaxation time is highly temperature-dependent.
explanations.d: Incorrect — It approaches an asymptote but never reaches absolute zero.

questions.question: Q9. What material property is strictly required to create a 'triple-shape' memory polymer?

answers.b: A polymer blend featuring two distinct glass transition temperatures.
answers.c: A polymer that responds to both heat and light.
answers.d: A highly crystalline metal alloy structure.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Color has no bearing on mechanical shape memory.
explanations.b: Correct — A phase-separated copolymer with two distinct T_g values enables two temporary shapes.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Triple-shape can be achieved purely thermally.
explanations.d: Incorrect — We are discussing polymers, not SMAs.

questions.question: Q10. Which physical state characterizes an amorphous polymer when it is below its T_g?

explanations.a: Incorrect — This is the state above T_g.
explanations.b: Incorrect — This is the state far above T_g.
explanations.c: Correct — Below T_g, the polymer chains are frozen in a rigid, glassy state.
